A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LINO UniPS and PS-Verse. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v3 reports original normal-estimation benchmarks, architectural ablations, PBR material prediction, and synthetic and real-image reconstruction results.

after.justification: v5 retains these empirical results and adds controlled component comparisons in Appendix A1.6, Tables A2–A4, and Figures A14–A16.

M1.justification: The proposed light registers, alignment supervision, interleaved attention, dual branches, normal-gradient loss, curriculum, and PBR extension are retained. Expanded fusion details document the existing architecture; the new appendix variants are experimental ablations rather than changes to the proposed model.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation coverage is retained: PS-Verse, PS-Mix, DiLiGenT, Luces, DiLiGenT102, DiLiGenT-Π failure examples, and real/mobile captures, including normal and PBR prediction. The added ablations use existing PS-Verse evaluation coverage. Point-only illumination was already illustrated in v3 despite its duplicated lighting-configuration label.

E2.justification: Appendix A1.6 adds internal comparison variants, including generic supervised registers, single-type registers, and single-branch models. Existing external comparator membership is unchanged: UniPS, SDM UniPS, Uni MS-PS, IDArb for PBR prediction, and PS-FCN/SDPS in the DiLiGenT102 comparison.

E3.justification: A1.6 introduces controlled comparisons against the final Table 2 model. Token experiments keep three registers while varying their specialization and associated supervision; branch experiments vary feature extraction while retaining other settings. Existing benchmark protocols and training budgets remain unchanged. The newly specified pairwise similarity averaging is a documentation clarification.

E4.justification: Beyond v3's cumulative component, decoder, and model-size ablations, v5 adds targeted tests of individual register types, specialized versus generic registers, and downsample-only versus wavelet-only versus dual branches. Tables A2–A4 and Figures A14–A16 substantially strengthen component-level analysis. Figure 6 also adds qualitative evidence for the retained cumulative ablation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The retained feature-variance visualizations and confidence-weighted loss do not constitute new uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New ablation results report MAEs of 5.32°, 5.30°, and 4.98° for Direction-, Env-, and Point-only register types; 5.07° for generic registers; and 5.98°/4.97° for downsample-only/wavelet-only branches, versus 4.51° for the full model. Qualitative comparisons are added. Existing benchmark and PBR scores remain unchanged, including 4.65° on DiLiGenT and 9.43° on Luces.

T1.justification: The mathematical method and losses are retained. Token-dimension and PBR loss-index corrections are notational. A1.4.1 adds rendering and encoder/decoder notation to express the existing inverse-problem motivation, without a new substantive derivation, formal guarantee, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, three listed contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about illumination decoupling, geometric-detail preservation, PS-Verse, generalization, accuracy, and efficiency. The introduction's correction from similar lighting features to similar normal features aligns terminology with the existing thesis.

C2.justification: A1.4.1 recasts feature consistency through illumination marginalization and decoder ill-posedness. A1.6 adds explanations involving point-light cues, generic-token entanglement, and complementary branch functions. A1.4.2 retains computational and normal-inversion limitations while adding data dependence and a clearer comparison with calibrated PS.

D1.justification: A1.1.4 specifies token reshaping, convolution sizes, strides, and progressive fusion operations; Section 4 specifies averaging CSIM/SSIM over all feature pairs. Notation and a duplicated lighting-configuration entry are corrected. The first-page Hugging Face Spaces demo link is removed, while project, code, and model links remain; this establishes an access-information change, not service unavailability.

R1.justification: v5 adds Glasner et al. (2009), Guo et al. (2017), and Zhang (2019) to support the branch rationale, plus StereoCarla and LightStereo references connecting dataset curation with stereo research. The main related-work positioning remains stable; these citations are not newly evaluated external baselines.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and section order are retained. Local revisions expand fusion, feature-consistency, and limitations explanations, standardize terminology, and correct attention descriptions and cross-references. A1.6 and acknowledgements are added; author order, affiliations, and the conference-paper header also change.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is reorganized, with its high-level pipeline moved into appendix Figure A1 and annotated with tensor shapes. v5 adds main Figure 6, appendix Figures A14–A16, and Tables A2–A4. Existing tables are repositioned and receive clearer metric captions/headers; retained appendix illustrations are renumbered.

improvement.justification: The controlled ablations in A1.6 address specific attribution gaps left by v3's cumulative ablation, strengthening support for token specialization and the dual branches. Fusion and metric clarifications improve reproducibility, and expanded limitations clarify applicability. These are useful incremental gains. Stronger invariance assertions in A1.4.1 remain only heuristically supported, and removal of the demo link modestly reduces access guidance.
